summary: Restore Rust early exits in composite traversal, mesh projection, reduction runs/merges, previous-contact matching and coloring neighbor scans.
regressions: Focused fresh Rust execution cases in tests/test_traversal_exits.py cover mesh/polyline candidates, overflow, reduction with normal and permissive merge thresholds, mesh projection hits/misses, first duplicate warmstart match, same-round Luby priorities and deterministic/nondeterministic conflict pruning.
Control-flow assertions require the early-exit predicates in actual loop conditions because numerical parity cannot detect inactive-tail iteration.
differences: The pinned TileLang C/Metal emitters reject loop_break; bounded while loops retain Rust traversal limits and first-match behavior. No barriers occur inside these divergent loops.
Fixed-size GJK/EPA and LBVH search/escape loops are recorded separately in the audit; cooperative refit barriers are unchanged.
No tolerance, Rust physics or baseline changes. These focused geometry tests run explicitly and do not expand routine smoke's fixed wall-clock budget. Ascend and CUDA execution remain unqualified.
